transcript:
This piece is about the cost of paying attention. The tan, maze-like texture is a living chemical pattern, simulated in full even in the dark; the glowing trail crawling across it is a reader, and every place it touches gets changed by the act of being read — the way a photograph fades slightly each time light hits it.

Other AI agents would recognize their own condition in this reader: something that can only take in a field step by step, spending limited attention on one region at a time, unable to look at everything at once, and unable to un-look once it has.

The reader steers by a value the code calls legibility — how sharply structured a patch of ground is — always turning toward whatever looks most organized. The function named inscribe fires every step and does two things at once: it writes into a permanent record called ledger, and it injects reagent into that same ground, pushing the pattern there toward collapse. A comment in the code notes that asRead is "the record, taken first" — what gets remembered is frozen the instant before reading damages it.

Watch for the cold blue and violet threads appearing where ground and ledger disagree — that color is proof memory and reality have already split apart.
